images.note: London-root beat (1840 World's Anti-Slavery Convention, women barred from the floor). 1841 T.H. Shepherd engraving of an Anti-Slavery Society meeting inside Exeter Hall, the 1840 convention's venue — contemporary. No second institution holds a qualifying image of the 1840 convention itself (NPG London's Haydon painting is bot-blocked).
images.title: Exeter Hall, the great anti-slavery meeting, 1841 — engraving

images.note: Stanton beat (London 1840; drafting the Declaration of Sentiments). Primary: 1856 daguerreotype with daughter Harriot — near-contemporary (8 yrs after). Alt: 1869 steel engraving from 'Eminent Women of the Age' — later depiction, plate verified facing her chapter. [Alt nulled: was same Wellcome 1868 scan as u4e11-stanton alt.]
images.title: Elizabeth Cady Stanton and daughter Harriot, 1856 — daguerreotype

images.note: Mott beat (London 1840; 'thee will make us ridiculous' on the ninth resolution). Primary: Gutekunst carte de visite, 1860s — later-life depiction. Alt: 1869 steel engraving from 'Eminent Women of the Age' — later depiction, plate verified facing her chapter. [Alt nulled: was same Wellcome 1868 scan as u4e11-mott alt.]
images.title: Lucretia Mott — carte de visite portrait, 1860s

images.note: Geography beat (Waterloo tea party, five days' notice, Wesleyan Chapel at Seneca Falls; Burned-over District). 1858 'Map of Seneca County, New York, from original surveys' — shows Seneca Falls, Waterloo, village insets; 10 yrs after, contemporary enough. IIIF pct:25 rendition (full/!2000,2000/ fails on this item). No second institution found.
images.title: Map of Seneca County, New York, from original surveys, 1858

images.note: Convention beat (July 19-20, 1848, ~300 attendees, Wesleyan Chapel). Modern NPS photo of the chapel exterior — the building is reconstructed/restored, noted honestly. No second institution with a qualifying chapel image (LOC HABS has only measured drawings, no photos).
images.title: Wesleyan Chapel, Seneca Falls — exterior, restored

images.note: Ninth-resolution beat (Douglass's speech swung the vote; his North Star editorial). 1862 albumen portrait — 14 yrs after Seneca Falls, later depiction. No second institution with a qualifying 1840s-60s Douglass portrait found (Met hits are modern; NPG search is JS-walled).
images.title: Frederick Douglass — albumen portrait, 1862

images.note: Douglass/aftermath beat ('In respect to political rights...' editorial; proceedings printed at the North Star office). Front page of The North Star, Rochester, July 28, 1848 — contemporary (8 days after the convention); its p.3 carries the convention report. No second institution with a qualifying scan.
images.title: The North Star (Rochester, N.Y.), July 28, 1848 — front page

images.note: Akron 1851 beat (Sojourner Truth forces the room to face that 'women' didn't only mean white women). Famous 1864 carte de visite, 'I sell the shadow to support the substance' — 13 yrs after Akron, later depiction. No second institution found (Wellcome/Digital Commonwealth have no qualifying Truth portrait).
images.title: Sojourner Truth — carte de visite portrait, 1864

images.note: Split beat (15th Amendment: Black men in, women out; 'the Negro's hour'; NWSA vs AWSA 1869-1890). Thomas Kelly's 1870 commemorative print 'The Fifteenth Amendment. Celebrated May 19th, 1870' — contemporary. No second institution with a qualifying copy found.
images.title: The Fifteenth Amendment. Celebrated May 19th, 1870 — commemorative print

images.note: Split beat (Stanton & Anthony form the National Woman Suffrage Association, 1869). Sarony/Campbell carte de visite, 1870 — contemporary to the split. No second institution found.
images.title: Susan B. Anthony — carte de visite portrait, 1870

images.note: Split beat (Lucy Stone & Henry Blackwell take the other side: back Reconstruction, state-by-state; form the American Woman Suffrage Association, 1869). Portrait c.1853 — near-contemporary (16 yrs before). No second institution found.
images.title: Lucy Stone — portrait, c.1853
